name: 47 Tucanae
tagline: The sky's second-brightest globular cluster — a million-star swarm in the halo near the Small Magellanic Cloud's line of sight.
history: 47 Tucanae is the most massive globular cluster in the Milky Way after Omega Centauri — a dense spheroid of a million ancient stars packing a core where blue stragglers and millisecond pulsars thrive. It sits in the halo far above the disc, 14,500 light-years out, yet shines at magnitude 4 — bright enough to be a southern naked-eye landmark. Hubble has tracked its crowded heart for decades, revealing one of the richest populations of exotic binaries and pulsars of any known cluster.
